chunks: From al-Hasan ibn Hudhayfah, from his father, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, the people narrate among us that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) fasted like this and like this and like this,' and he gestured with his hand, bringing one hand to meet the other, [indicating] ten and ten and nine, which is more than what he fasted like this and like this and like this, meaning ten and ten and ten.

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not fast less than thirty days, and the month of Ramadan has not been less than thirty days since Allah created the heavens and the earth.'

And he mentioned it via another chain - from Abu Imran al-Munshid, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, by Allah, the month of Ramadan has not been less than, nor will it ever be less than, thirty days and thirty nights.'
So I said to Hudhayfah - perhaps he said to you 'thirty nights and thirty days' as the people say 'the night is the night of the day' - Hudhayfah said to me: 'I heard it like this.'
ai.seo_question: How many days is the month of Ramadan according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the notion that Ramadan's length varied by affirming it has remained a fixed thirty-day month since creation, thereby establishing the consistency of the lunar calendar in Shia jurisprudence. This narration serves as a critical counter to reports suggesting the Prophet fasted for shorter periods, reinforcing the theological certainty of Ramadan's duration as a divine ordinance rather than a variable practice.
